date: Approx. 30-35 H (650-656); his killing: Dhu al-Hijja 35 H (June 656)
title: 11zh5hi
The Era of Caliph Uthman, the Siege of Medina and Imam Ali
hook: As complaints grew, Imam Ali mediated in Medina. Afterwards, the pledge of allegiance was demanded of him.
scenes.0.text: C**aliph** Uthman's first years in Medina were peaceful. However, in the second half of his caliphate, governorships and state property became the subject of a major complaint. Important duties were given to each of the Umayyad sons, the caliph's own relatives. Before Kufa, Walid b. Ukbe, then **Said b. As** was sent as governor. **Abdullah b. Sa'd** was brought to Egypt, **Abdullah b. Amir** to Basra. **Mervan** took over as the Caliph's secretary. In the reign of Umar, Mu'awiya's jurisdiction was extended to include Homs, Kinnesrin, and Palestine. The people were talking about large donations to relatives and rulers from the common treasury of the nation. Ali saw this move as harmful to the Ummah and openly criticized the caliph.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.1.text: Complaints moved from the regions to Medina over time. Then there came to him a delegation from Egypt, and from Khufa, and from Basra. They complained about the oppression of the governors, the appointments of the Emvites, and the arbitrary use of the common treasure called Beitülmal. The streets of Medina filled with the angry voices of these delegations. People were talking about what was happening in the mosque, in the marketplace and in their homes. Tension was rising in the city, and everyone wondered how this would turn out. In the midst of this crowd, **Ali** was the confidant of both the caliph and the people.
scenes.2.text: **Ali** went to Caliph Uthman and conveyed to him the complaints of the people one by one and asked him to change his attitude. When the Egyptian delegation approached Medina, at Uthman's request, Ali and Muhammad b. Mesleme went to meet them. After a lengthy discussion, it was promised that the complaints would be resolved. The delegation went back, trusting in that word. Ali's goal was to prevent bloodshed in the city of the Prophet. So he stood between the two sides and tried to calm both the caliph and the people. Medina took a breath for a moment.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.3.text: But that deal was quickly broken. Ali had warned the caliph against **Mervan** earlier and said he would leave Uthman in a difficult position. He advised her to stay away from Mervan. Ali's advice was not followed. As the Egyptians were returning home, they saw a horseman hurrying toward Egypt. According to the history books, this man was a slave of the caliph and rode on his camel. When they searched it, they found a letter addressed to the governor of Egypt, **Abdullah b. Sa'd**, and sealed with the caliph's seal. The letter ordered that the leaders of the delegation be killed or severely punished upon their arrival in Egypt. So the promise was broken in Medina, and a trap was laid for the complainers. The Egyptians took the letter and returned to Medina in anger. Caliph Uthman swore he didn't write the letter. The seal and the camel belonged to him, but since he was the Caliph's secretary who handled the correspondence, doubts gathered on him. The identity of the writer of the letter is still debated, and no one can be sure. The Egyptians demanded that Mervan be handed over to them, but the caliph refused. No one could convince them this time. The Caliph's house fell into a siege that would last for days.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.3.art.actors.2.label: sbbh7k
Marwan
scenes.4.text: Uthman, who put aside the pleasure of Allah and preferred the pleasure of his relatives and those around him, finally faced the consequences of this at his doorstep. When the siege began, C**aliph** Uthman retreated to his home. The house was surrounded by an armed mob. Getting water and food in became increasingly difficult. He said to his companions, "The Prophet has taken a promise from me. I am patient with him". The anger of the besiegers in the streets of Medina grew a little bit more every day. Ali kept trying to avoid bloodshed in the midst of all this confusion. Despite years of denial, he refused to accept the caliph's death.
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.5.text: During the siege, **Ali** sent his two sons, **Hasan** and Husayn, to guard the door of Uthman's house. It is also said that he tried to bring water to the besieged house. Some accounts say that Hasan was wounded in the process. Muhammad Ali, who had been declared the rightful ruler of Ghadir and sidelined for years, had sent his own sons to the gate to protect a caliph who had succeeded him. He didn't approve of the rebels' sword. For him, the shedding of a Muslim's blood in the city of the Prophet was a greater matter than his own.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.5.art.actors.2.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.art.actors.3.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.6.text: Despite all these efforts, C**aliph** Uthman was assassinated in his home in Medina on the 18th of Zilhicce, in the 35th year of the Hijrah. His caliphate lasted about twelve years. Ali later described the incident in a sermon: If he had ordered his death, he would have been considered a murderer. If he could keep people away from him, he'd be his assistant. He said he left the decision to God. Ali did not use a sword in this murder, nor was he involved in this bloodshed. Uthman's body was buried in Baku, and Medina fell into a great earthquake.
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: After Uthman's death, Medina was left without a ruler for several days. There was fear and uncertainty in the city. Finally, the people came to **Ali**'s door and asked him to accept the caliphate. Ali knew how difficult this task was. What he was about to overthrow was no ordinary state. He was to take over a quarter-century of unjust governance, distribution of property to the undeserving and favoritism. The crowd gathered at the mosque and Ali was beheaded there. A pledge of allegiance. The man who raised his hand at Ghadir, after almost a quarter of a century passed, went before the Ummah. This time it was the people themselves who wanted it.

Imam Ali
sunni.0.says: Caliph Uthman on the day of the siege: "The Messenger of God took a pledge from me, and I am bearing it with patience."
sunni.0.grade: Tirmidhi: hasan sahih; Albani and Ali al-Za'i: sahih (Sufyan b. Waki' in the chain is weak, there is a supporting narration)
sunni.1.says: Caliph Uthman is given the glad tidings of Paradise in return for a calamity that will befall him.
sunni.2.says: The delegations, the siege and his killing are narrated in detail.
sunni.3.says: Imam Hasan's wounding and Imam Ali's stance are included in this account.
sunni.4.says: Caliph Uthman's caliphate, the delegations and the siege.
sunni.5.says: The narration that Imam Ali assigned Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn to guard Caliph Uthman's house.
shia.0.says: Ali: If I had ordered the murderer, if I had prevented it, I would have helped. Judgment belongs to Allah.
shia.1.says: Imam Ali describes how his right was brushed aside in the period before him.
shia.2.says: The Shia account of the events before the Camel.
shia.3.says: Relates narrations about the killing of Caliph Uthman.
shia.4.says: The matter of Caliph Uthman's blood and the correspondence between Imam Ali and Mu'awiya.
shia.5.says: Views that find the narration weak because of problems in the chain are relayed.
disputes.0.title: f08mf2
Were Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn at the house?
disputes.0.sunni: The narration of guarding and Imam Hasan's wounding are mentioned in some Sunni books (Baladhuri, Ansab al-Ashraf; Ibn Kathir, al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya). In the Sunni reading, it is also noted that Imam Ali had no control over the rebels.
disputes.0.shia: The narration of guarding is also mentioned in Baladhuri. Some Shia scholars find the chain weak; that Imam Ali did not support the siege, and the extent of his help to Caliph Uthman, are also separately discussed.
disputes.1.title: o63fch
Imam Ali's stance
disputes.1.sunni: Imam Ali warned Caliph Uthman and mediated so that the strife would not grow. The judgment of those involved in this matter later became a subject of debate.
disputes.1.shia: Imam Ali conveyed the complaints and mediated. In the Shia reading, he saw them as justified, did not approve of the shedding of blood, and left the judgment to God.
questions.0: Ali conveyed the people's complaints to Caliph Uthman and went to meet the Egyptian delegation. Why do you think Ali stood between the two sides, trying to calm both the caliph and the people?
questions.1: Caliph Uthman under siege said, "The Prophet took a promise from me, I am patient with it". Why do you think Caliph Uthman chose patience instead of taking a step back?
questions.2: In his sermon, Ali said that if the Caliph had ordered the killing of Uthman, the killer would have been his assistant if he could have stopped people. Why do you think Ali described his attitude at the time in these two ways?
questions.3: The tradition that Hasan and Husayn were sent to protect the house of Caliph Uthman is considered weak by some scholars. Why is a rumor that you consider weak still being told when it's Ali's look at the bloodshed?
questions.4: Ali assumed the caliphate knowing that he was taking over the ruins of a quarter-century of rule. Why do you think Ali started fixing the unfair governor appointments and the unfair distribution of wealth?
summary: The complaints in the second half of Caliph Uthman's reign led to the siege and his killing in 35 H. Imam Ali mediated. Uthman said, "The Prophet took a pledge from me, and I am bearing it with patience." When the people ran to him, Imam Ali took on the caliphate knowingly and began to establish justice.
key: The era of the third caliph and growing unrest
notes.0: Caliph Uthman's first years passed calmly; in the second half, governorships and the distribution of wealth became a subject of complaint.
notes.1: Delegations came to Medina from Egypt, Kufa and Basra with complaints.
notes.3: Medina was besieged and Caliph Uthman was killed in Dhu al-Hijja 35 H.
notes.4: Afterwards the people came to Imam Ali and asked him to accept their pledge of allegiance.
